title: Thai Green Curry
subtitle: fragrant Thai coconut curry with chicken and green beans
excerpt: Thai green curry gets its colour and heat from fresh green chillies blended into the paste. The coconut milk tempers the heat and adds richness. It is one of the most fragrant dishes in Thai cooking and comes together quickly once the paste is made.
sourceNotes: Thai green curry (gaeng keow wan) is thought to have emerged in central Thailand in the early twentieth century. The paste is made from green chillies, lemongrass, galangal, and kaffir lime leaves, among other aromatics. The dish became internationally known through Thai immigration and the global spread of Thai restaurants.

content.text: The paste is the foundation of this curry. If you use a shop-bought green curry paste, fry it in oil for 2 minutes before adding the chicken -- this step removes the raw flavour. Making a quick paste from scratch takes 5 minutes and tastes noticeably fresher.

items.prepNote: use a 400ml tin of coconut milk
use 3 lemongrass stalks, bruised and knotted -- and 4 kaffir lime leaves
sliced -- or use galangal if available
use 2 to 4 fresh green chillies if available -- blend with the aromatics
juice of half a lime -- to finish

content.text: Make the curry paste: blend the garlic, ginger (or galangal), chilli, and a splash of oil to a rough paste. For a more traditional paste, add shallots and lemongrass stalks (remove the tough outer layers first).
Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat. Fry the paste for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chicken pieces. Stir to coat in the paste. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes until sealed.
Pour in the coconut milk and stock. Add the lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and fish sauce. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the green beans. Simmer for 10 to 12 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the beans are tender.
Squeeze in the lime juice. Remove the lemongrass. Serve with jasmine rice and fresh coriander.

items.cause: Too many chillies in the paste
items.fix: Add more coconut milk to temper the heat. A little honey or brown sugar also helps balance fire. Next time, use fewer chillies and taste the paste before cooking with it.

content.text: Thai green curry is the most internationally exported Thai dish after pad Thai. In Thailand it is made with small, fierce green chillies. The balance of fish sauce, lime, and coconut milk is what makes it distinctively Thai. Jasmine rice is the only accompaniment needed.
